old_crew_documentary.title: The Crew He Left Behind
old_crew_documentary.//: Story Phase 17 (chapter 212): a Stenchmaster Channel documentary, on the galley's set. What became of a crew after their captain died: the books, the orders, the chair on deck, the last years. Viewer comments between its parts; the set notices who's watching. Original material.

beats.line: documentary_narrator: The Stenchmaster Channel presents: THE CREW HE LEFT BEHIND.
documentary_narrator: When their captain died, his crew did what crews do. They went on. Badly, but they went on.
documentary_narrator: Ledger Billiam kept the books. Money in one. Their captain's wind in the other. He went on entering it as an asset for twenty-one years.
documentary_narrator: No-Nonsense Tilda kept order. She ran the ship. She shouted at the crew every day, as he would have wanted. There was less crew every year to shout at.
documentary_narrator: And every evening, when the work was done, she went up on deck and sat beside his chair.
documentary_narrator: She told the chair everything he'd done wrong that day. He hadn't done anything. He'd been dead for years. She told it anyway.
documentary_narrator: Eleven years. The chair never said 'Tilda, stop'. She stopped anyway, in the end.
documentary_narrator: Old Jeb sold the last of the ship, some of it twice. Wobbly Ned wobbled off a quay in Port Cramp and nobody saw him again. Elsie cooked beans until the very last morning.
documentary_narrator: Ledger was the last. Very old, very cold, in a bed in a port nobody remembers. He told the woman holding his hand where the books were.
documentary_narrator: A sea chest, he said. Greyhook Cove. Keep them safe. Somebody will want to know what he was worth.
documentary_narrator: (very slowly) ...Tilda. Is that you? Watching?
documentary_narrator: Sit up straight. (a pause) He'd have liked to see you again. (a pause) Oh. He has.
documentary_narrator: THE CREW HE LEFT BEHIND. Thank you for watching. All three of you.
